images.title: Joining strips adds the exponents
images.purpose: Shows p⁴ and p to the power 6 joined into one strip of 10 p's, so the exponents add.
images.composition: Plain white background, lots of empty space around the main object, no scenery, no people, no extra text. Two short strips of blocks on the top line and one long joined strip below them, with a downward arrow between.
images.exact_structure: Top line: a strip of exactly 4 teal (#0072B2) square blocks each showing 'p', labelled 'p⁴' above it; a small gap; a strip of exactly 6 amber (#E69F00) square blocks each showing 'p', labelled 'p⁶' above it. A thick grey downward arrow in the middle. Bottom line: one joined strip of exactly 10 blocks touching edge to edge, the first 4 teal (#0072B2) and the next 6 amber (#E69F00), each showing 'p'. A reddish purple (#CC79A7) brace under the whole bottom strip with the label 'p¹⁰' under it, and the label '4 + 6 = 10' beside the brace. Exactly 20 blocks in all, 1 arrow, 1 brace.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
images.takeaway: Multiplying powers of the same base adds the exponents.
images.description: Shows p⁴ and p to the power 6 joined into one strip of 10 p's, so the exponents add.
images.context: p⁴ × p to the power 6 gives p to the power 10; also 2⁴ × 2 to the power 5 is 16 × 32 = 512, which is 2 to the power 9.
images.teaching_notes: Label 'p' appears on all 20 blocks. Contrast with the wrong answer p to the power 24.

image_decisions.why: Joining two strips of the same base into one longer strip is exactly why the exponents add.
